script.title: Jay Gould tried to corner America's gold. Then Grant acted 🤯
sentences: In 1869, Jay Gould set out to corner America's gold.
His partners were Jim Fisk and President Grant's own brother-in-law, Abel Corbin.
Gould even opened a $500,000 gold account for Grant's secretary, Horace Porter.
By September 22, Gould and Fisk held about three times New York's public gold supply.
Then Porter told Grant about that account.
On Friday, September 24, Grant released $4 million in government gold.
The price collapsed, Wall Street panicked, and the day became known as Black Friday.
Gould and Fisk hired the best defense available and escaped prosecution.
script.description:
The original Black Friday: a gold corner, a president's brother-in-law and a crash in 1869.
How Jay Gould and Jim Fisk nearly owned America's gold.
claims_en: In 1869 Jay Gould sought to corner the gold market.
Gould was joined by James Fisk and Abel Corbin, President Grant's brother-in-law.
Gould opened a $500,000 gold account in the name of Grant's personal secretary Horace Porter.
Porter refused the offer in writing.
On September 22 Fisk and Gould owned about three times the public supply of gold available in New York.
Porter told Grant about Gould setting up the account, and Grant realized what Gould and Fisk were up to.
On September 24, 1869 (a Friday), Grant ordered the release of $4 million in government gold.
The move drove down the price of gold, a panic on Wall Street followed, and the panic became known as Black Friday.
Gould and Fisk hired the best defense available and escaped prosecution.
scenes: Extreme close-up of 1869 financier Jay Gould's face, dark beard, intense calculating eyes and a thin confident smile, lit by gaslight in a Wall Street office.
Medium shot of three 1869 businessmen in frock coats, the dark-bearded Jay Gould, the flamboyant Jim Fisk and the older Abel Corbin, talking quietly in a lavish gaslit parlour.
Close-up of Jay Gould sliding an open brokerage ledger across a polished desk with a sly expression, gold coins stacked beside it, 1869 office interior.
Medium shot of Horace Porter, a stern young former army officer in a dark suit, writing a firm refusal letter at a desk, jaw set, window light.
Wide shot of the crowded New York Gold Room in 1869, traders in top hats shouting and waving papers under a high ceiling, Gould and Fisk calm in the middle.
Medium shot of Horace Porter speaking urgently to President Ulysses S. Grant, bearded and grim in a dark suit, as Grant's expression hardens, afternoon light through tall windows.
Medium shot of President Grant signing an order at a desk in 1869, jaw clenched, a telegraph clerk waiting beside him.
Wide shot of panic on Wall Street in September 1869, crowds of men in frock coats spilling into the street, papers flying, grey overcast sky.
Medium shot of Jay Gould and Jim Fisk walking out of a courthouse in 1869 New York with their lawyers, Gould expressionless, Fisk smirking.
